focus: Ponytail command and skill delegation vs sk-code routing and the review output contract
noveltyJustification: 4 fully new output-contract and honesty mechanisms (skip-consequence bullet, not-checked closer, lean summary, anti-fabricated baseline), 2 partially new (traversal order, removal artifact classes), 3 already-adopted or rejected (routing stronger, no-code enforced, doctrine duplication rejected).
keyQuestions: How do Ponytail's commands and bundled skills delegate work (review, audit, gain, debt, help), and how does that compare with sk-code's mode-registry and hub-router routing?
answeredQuestions: How do Ponytail's commands and bundled skills delegate work (review, audit, gain, debt, help), and how does that compare with sk-code's mode-registry and hub-router routing?
ruledOut: Copying Ponytail's command-plus-skill doctrine duplication (contradicts the one-baseline rule)
Treating a lean summary line as a severity gate (prior LOC rejection stands; report-only evidence only)

graphEvents.label: Ponytail command delegation vs sk-code routing

label: Ponytail's four-bullet finding format carries an If-we-skip-it consequence field that sk-code-review's schema lacks; Risk and User impact describe the defect, not the cost of deferring the fix. Classification: NEW (additive schema row).

Ponytail review and audit both end with a Not checked section naming what mattered but was not examined; sk-code-review's output contract ends with Next Steps and the exact Review status line, with no review-coverage-limit section. Classification: NEW.

A report-only Lean: -N lines / -M dependencies summary line has no sk-code-review equivalent and stays compatible with the prior LOC-as-gate rejection because it is supporting evidence, not a severity input. Classification: NEW (report-only).

The gain command forbids per-repo savings numbers because the unbuilt version was never written, and declares itself one-shot with no persistence; this anti-fabricated-baseline rule is the honesty guard any sk-code restraint metric must carry. Classification: NEW (benchmark reporting rule).

Ponytail duplicates one doctrine across a five-line command paragraph and a multi-section skill file and lists the same names as both commands and skills; sk-code's one-baseline rule and single-source routing make that duplication the wrong pattern, leaving only the runtime-shim idea separable. Classification: REJECT (reasoned).

sk-code's two-stage registry routing (hub-router stage one, ROUTER.md surface-first intent-second stage two with a machine-readable projection) plus compiled routing with a legacy sentinel and kill-switch has no Ponytail counterpart; Ponytail commands are direct prompts with no routing layer. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (stronger).

Ponytail names a fixed review traversal order (correct, safe, holds under load, tested, fast, lean) independent of output severity ordering; sk-code-review orders output by severity but names no fixed check-pass order. Classification: NEW (partially; cheap additive).

Ponytail's audit names the artifact classes to grep before calling code unused (tests, fixtures, config, string references); sk-code-review's removal plan requires a completed codebase reference search but does not enumerate those classes. Classification: NEW (partially).

Ponytail's change-no-code rule is prose; sk-code-review enforces it structurally by forbidding Edit in its registry toolSurface and scoping Write to an untracked review cache. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (stronger).
